face: You come to my hearth asking for a pact? Your word has been weighed in every market of Ormerath, {player}, and found wanting. Keep your offer and your smile.
An alliance with you? I would sooner bind my cloak to a thornbush and trust the wind to hold it. No, ser {player}.
Ha! You name yourself my ally while your banners still drip with the blood of my kin. Begone before I remember that debt.
My ancestors sleep beneath stones you have never wept over. Speak of alliance again and I will answer with steel rather than ink.
No. Let {rival} court your favour if such things still tempt them. I have no wish to share my table with a name so easily sold.
Your proposal insults the oath I swore at my father's grave, and I will not dishonour that grave for your convenience, ser {player}.
A pact with you would last only until the next purse was counted. Take your parchment elsewhere and let the crows read it.
You offer friendship the way a wolf offers its heart to a lamb. Keep the gift for someone foolish enough to accept it.
I have heard your proposal, ser {player}, and I must decline it. My banner is not yet ready to lean on another's shield.
An alliance is a heavy thing to carry on a single handshake. I think we shall both be better served walking separate roads for now.
You are welcome to rest at this fire tonight, but I will not swear myself to you on the strength of one fair evening's talk.
Thank you for the offer. My council has not yet weighed the matter, and until it does, my answer stands as no.
Friendship is a fine thing, but oaths are finer, and I have not yet seen cause to swear one to you, ser {player}.
I would rather keep my options open than bind my fate to yours. Should that change, you will hear it from my own mouth.
Your words are pleasant enough. Still, I have made it a rule never to pledge my people to strangers, and you remain one.
No alliance today. Perhaps tomorrow, when the roads have told me more of you, and the roads are slow to tell the truth.
Ser {player}, it grieves me to refuse you, for I count you among the few who have earned a seat at my table. Not yet, though.
Your offer honours me, truly it does. But my vows are not mine to give away lightly, and I must ask you to be patient with me.
Would that I could say yes this very hour, ser {player}. My house is not in a position to bind itself to any banner just now.
You have stood by my side when the wolves came down from the hills, and so I owe you plain speech. I cannot swear this pact, not yet.
Friend, let us not sour the evening over parchment. Our hearts are already allied; it is only the formal oath that must wait for better days.
I refuse with a heavy heart. The council will not hear of it this season, but I shall keep your name first in my prayers and my plans.
Hear me, ser {player}: the answer is no for now, but never let it be said I turned my back on a friend. Share a cup with me instead.
A pact between us would be a fine tale for the minstrels, but I dare not stake my house on it until the storms of this season have passed.
